# Upstream fixtures

Recorded, trimmed snapshots of `https://json.tarkov.dev` used by the pipeline tests and, later, by
normalization golden tests. Everything here is committed so `npm test` runs offline.

Generated by `pipeline/src/scripts/capture-fixtures.ts`:

```bash
cd pipeline
npm run fixtures
```

## Layout

```
test/fixtures/upstream/
  common/
    status.json            GET /status
    manifest.json
  regular/
    items.json             GET /regular/items
    items_en.json          filtered GET /regular/items_en
    tasks.json             GET /regular/tasks
    tasks_en.json
    traders.json           GET /regular/traders
    traders_en.json
    hideout.json           GET /regular/hideout
    hideout_en.json
    crafts.json            GET /regular/crafts (no translations upstream)
    barters.json           GET /regular/barters (no translations upstream)
    maps.json              GET /regular/maps
    maps_en.json
    prices/<itemId>.json   GET /regular/prices/<itemId> (M4A1)
    manifest.json
  pve/
    items.json             3 mode-marker records
    items_en.json          dictionary entries for those records only
    manifest.json
  pvp-season/
    items.json             3 mode-marker records
    items_en.json          dictionary entries for those records only
    season.json            GET /pvp-season/season
    season_en.json
    manifest.json
```

Every dataset fixture keeps the upstream envelope shape `{ "data": ..., "translations": [...] }`
with **placeholder text still unresolved**. The matching `_en.json` is a dictionary
`{ "data": { "<placeholder>": "<text>" } }`. This is intentional: tests run `localizeInPlace` over
each pair and prove localization coverage instead of trusting already-resolved text.

## Trimming policy

- **Record selection is deterministic.** Records are sorted by `id`/`name` (then canonical JSON) and
  selected by `pipeline/src/fixtures/trim.ts`:
  - items: 60 records, one per distinct `propertiesType` + property-key shape, then filled by id;
  - tasks: 80 records, one per task shape, objective type/key shape (all 20 objective types and
    30 objective key shapes) and reward/requirement shape (all 40 `finishRewards` variants), then
    filled by id;
  - maps: 2 maps, one with and one without `artillery`, plus 2 representative `mobs` records;
  - crafts and barters: first 20 by id;
  - traders and hideout: every record (small datasets);
  - `pve` and `pvp-season` items: first 3 by id, kept as mode markers.
- **No key is dropped from a retained record.** Only long arrays are truncated. Array truncation keeps
  the first occurrence of every structural shape, then fills from the front, so nested shapes needed by
  the schemas survive.
- **Dictionaries are filtered** to the placeholder strings that still occur in the trimmed records.
  `pve/items_en.json` is therefore a few kilobytes, not a copy of the 17 MB regular dictionary
  (`pve/items_en` is byte-identical upstream; only the retained subset is stored).
- **Object keys are sorted recursively** and files are written with a trailing newline, so identical
  upstream data produces byte-identical fixture files. `manifest.json` is the exception: it records
  `fetchedAt`/`capturedAt`, which change on every capture.
- **Price history** keeps the most recent 120 observations (of ~1,840) for
  `5447a9cd4bdc2dbd208b4567`.

## Intentionally incomplete

- Items, tasks, maps, mobs, crafts and barters are subsets, not full datasets.
- Arrays inside retained records are truncated (6 elements for items and mode markers, 8 for tasks and
  hideout, 10 for maps, traders and the season, 6 for crafts/barters).
- Auxiliary item collections (`itemCategories`, `handbookCategories`, `fleaMarket`, `armorMaterials`,
  `playerLevels`, `mastering`, `skills`, `specialItems`, `settings`) are kept whole because they are
  small and referenced by translation pointers.
- The `pve` and `pvp-season` markers only prove mode scoping (the same item ids carry different price
  fields); they do not duplicate the regular catalog.

## Stale translation pointers

Each manifest entry lists `unresolvedPointers`, `failedPointers` and `missingKeys` measured **after**
trimming. Tests assert zero missing dictionary keys and zero unparsable pointers, and compare the
stale-pointer list exactly against the manifest. Known causes:

- Upstream metadata is already stale: `$.data.armorMaterial.*.name` and
  `$.data.fleaMarket.*.name` for items; the 13 `$.data.story.*` / reward-customization pointers for
  tasks.
- Trimming removes the matched nodes: item `zones`/`armorSlots`/`content`/`stimEffects` pointers for
  the 3-record mode markers, task `zones`/reward-customization pointers, and map `btrStops` for the
  selected maps.

If upstream adds a real dictionary gap, the localization test fails on `missingKeys` rather than
silently accepting placeholder text.

## Normalized goldens

`test/fixtures/normalized/<dataset>.jsonl` holds the byte-for-byte output of
`pipeline/src/normalize/` for each committed regular fixture. They are generated
offline by localizing the fixture and running `npm run normalize -- --all --out
../test/fixtures/normalized`. `npm test` compares every dataset against its
golden; update a golden only after reviewing the diff, since it is the bundle
contract. See [`docs/data-bundles.md`](../../docs/data-bundles.md).

## Budget

The whole directory must stay under **2,000,000 bytes** on disk. The test suite enforces this, and the
capture script prints the total plus the largest files.

## Refreshing

```bash
cd pipeline
npm run fixtures      # rewrites test/fixtures/upstream/
npm test              # validates localization, manifests, sizes and shapes offline
```

If an endpoint fails, the script skips it, reports the source and reason, records it under `skipped`
in that fixture set's manifest, and never fabricates data. Review the diff and the manifests before
committing.
